fields.bio:
I am a Senior Scientist and Leader of the Rock Mechanics Group at the Chair of Engineering Geology and Hydrogeology, RWTH Aachen University. My research focuses on rock mechanics, rock engineering design and numerical modelling, applied to rock slope and landslide analysis and to underground infrastructure, from the laboratory to the in-situ scale.

I have been principal investigator and co-investigator on national and international projects on deep geological repositories, rock slope stability and landslide analysis, geohazard assessment and underground excavation design.

I teach Soil & Rock Mechanics, Landslides and Rock Slope Analysis, Underground Excavation, Dams and Hydroelectric Power Plants, and field excursions. I am a member of the International Society for Rock Mechanics (ISRM) and the American Rock Mechanics Association (ARMA), and a reviewer for Rock Mechanics and Rock Engineering, Landslides, and the Journal of Rock Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering.

fields.title: Progressive Excavation Disturbance Zone Evolution during and Post Mine-by Tunnelling (PRECODE)
fields.summary: A 100 m experimental tunnel branching off the Bedretto tunnel in Ticino, Switzerland, instrumented to monitor strain, pore pressure and micro-seismicity. The project studies how the excavation damage zone forms and evolves, long-term fracture propagation, permeability changes and the impact on fault zones. Partners: York University, Dalhousie University, ETH Zurich and BGE Tech.

fields.title: Understanding Failure Mechanism of Non-Persistent Discontinuities Using 3D-Printed Synthetic Rock Mass
fields.summary: Laboratory tests on 3D-printed synthetic rock mass samples with known joint configurations, used to calibrate numerical models and develop a constitutive model for rock mass strength. In collaboration with GeoPrint at the University of Alberta, Canada.

fields.title: Landslide Dam Properties and Stability (LADY)
fields.summary: Why do some landslide dams remain stable for thousands of years while others fail within months? LADY combines dam mapping, lake water-balance analysis and numerical stability simulations to test a new hypothesis.
